eyebrow: ServiceNow Security & Access Controls · Chapter Four
subtitle: Lesson 12 · Data Protection & Encryption

eyebrow: The gap roles and ACLs can't close
code:
Roles, ACLs, SSO, MFA:            The remaining gap:
- control WHO reaches data         - once written, ServiceNow
- control HOW they authenticate      itself can read the value
- don't change who holds the key   - some fields need stronger
                                      confidentiality than that
caption: Access control and confidentiality are different problems.

eyebrow: Edge Encryption: encrypt before it leaves the customer's network
code:
Without Edge Encryption:            With Edge Encryption:
Browser -> ServiceNow cloud          Browser -> customer's edge proxy
  (plaintext reaches                   (encrypted HERE, in the
   ServiceNow's servers)                customer's own network)
                                      -> ServiceNow cloud
                                        (only ciphertext arrives)
caption: Same spirit as the MID Server pattern: processing stays in the customer's network.

eyebrow: The result: the vendor never holds the plaintext
code:
ServiceNow's cloud, support staff,
and infrastructure never see the
plaintext of an Edge-Encrypted field.

Only the customer's own environment
ever holds the real value and the keys.
caption: The capability to look is never present on the vendor's side.

eyebrow: Column-level encryption: a narrower, simpler control
code:
Edge Encryption:                    Column-level encryption:
- encrypts in customer's network    - encrypts at rest in the DB
- vendor never sees plaintext       - app layer still decrypts
- defends against the cloud           to use the value
  vendor itself                     - defends against storage
                                       exposure (e.g. a backup)
caption: Different threats, different guarantees.
